The circles $r=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $r=1$ intersect for $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ at points $A$ and $B,$ as shown above. What are the polar coordinates $({r}_{A},{\theta }_{A})$ and $({r}_{B},{\theta }_{B})$ of the points $A$ and $B,$ respectively? Express the polar angles ${\theta }_{A}$ and ${\theta }_{B}$ in radians.

$({r}_{A},{\theta }_{A})=(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$),\,$

$({r}_{B},{\theta }_{B})=(${{field-3}}$,$
{{field-4}}$)$
question.worked_solution:
To determine the polar coordinates of the intersection points, we will solve the following system of equations for $r$ and $\theta :$  

$$
\{\begin{aligned}r=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ r=1\end{aligned}
$$

We begin by setting the equations equal to each other and solve for $\theta .$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation in the interval $[0,2\pi ),$ we obtain ${\theta }_{1}=\frac{2\pi }{3}$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{4\pi }{3}.$

Also, notice that $r=1$ at both intersection points.

Therefore, the polar coordinates $({r}_{A},{\theta }_{A})$ and $({r}_{B},{\theta }_{B})$ of the points $A$ and $B,$ respectively, are

$$
({r}_{A},{\theta }_{A})=(1,\frac{2\pi }{3}),\,({r}_{B},{\theta }_{B})=(1,\frac{4\pi }{3}).
$$
